title: Manhasset
summary: Manhasset names the village and neck formerly called Cow Neck in present-day Nassau County.
map_geometry_source: Approximate modern Manhasset village center used for a general placename marker.
introduction_content: Manhasset is a modern Nassau County placename for a village and the former Cow Neck area near Manhasset Bay. It is presented here as a later western Long Island use of a name related to Manhansett of Shelter Island.
history_content: Earlier interpretations applied the Manhansett name to Cow Neck. Manhasset is a later cross-reference to Manhansett rather than evidence of a separate Indigenous land name for Cow Neck.
translation_content:
The history derives Manhasset from Manhansett. Manhansett is interpreted as island land or neighborhood, so this Manhasset entry is best treated as a transferred or altered form rather than a separate translation rooted in the Cow Neck landscape.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are traces left behind by people. Behind each name is a story of human interaction, showcasing the experiences and perspectives of interweaving cultures.”

— National Museum of Taiwan History, Place Names Tell Stories (n.d.), exhibition introduction
whereintheworld_content: Manhasset is shown at the modern village in relation to Manhasset Bay and the former Cow Neck. The location does not define an exact historic boundary.
